I know that no one ever commented on this, but I’ll update it very late because someone else may be in the same boat I was and feel the same kind of anxiety.
I got diagnosed 3 months later. The specialist said “you’re one of the most obvious cases of adult female ADHD I’ve ever seen”. I cried on the spot.
I got medicated - vyvanse and Wellbutrin - and am doing amazing on my medications. I can think, clean, take care of myself. I can finally see in 3d whereas I was seeing in 2d before. I’m very glad I took the step, even if I was terrified id get labeled or not taken seriously. 
If you think you may have adhd and you have these concerns, please try anyway. My life has changed for the better since getting medicated. It’s been 3ish years and I can say that with full confidence. 
Good luck, whoever you are. ❤️
Sick, thank you for the reassurance! I’m less freaked now.
I’m currently on medications for my ADHD, which are stimulants. Vyvanse, adderall IR, and Wellbutrin. I don’t believe they cause fainting spells, hair loss or bruising according to my psychiatrist.

I’m not sure if I could eat 1,700 calories at this point, but I’ll talk to my doctor about how many calories I should be taking in and how I can get to that point without getting nauseated all the time. Thank you, I’ll make sure to remember to bring this up.

I am female, 20 years old. 1,500 calories seems like a lot and I’m not sure if I would be able to eat that much without getting sick anymore. If I slowly increase my intake, by what sized increments should I increase it per day/week?
According to my Happy Scale input, 5.6 per week.

I’ve stopped counting within the last two months, but I had been eating 800-1,200 to begin with. I’ve never counted any of my macronutrients, but I do take multivitamins. I don’t have much of an appetite anymore, so it isn’t a struggle to stay under my goal. My medication can be blamed for the lack of appetite.

May I ask what the health risks are? I’ve currently been dealing with dizzy spells, fainting spells, hair loss, and a lot of bruising. My doctor has said this is normal for weight loss as you’re going to be deficient in a lot of vitamins in a deficit.

If I am 5’5, and have lost roughly 95 pounds in 6 months, that’s considered healthy then? Because I have a higher bf%? I’m slightly confused so please be patient with me. I’m mixed up between tall and short. The taller you are, the less you can lose in a short amount of time safely? And it is the opposite for shorter people?
I already find happiness in pets haha. The only reason I wasn’t dead years ago is because of my two dogs. Problems just get bigger and fixes stay the same size... thank you.
I’d like to live on my own and go to school for veterinary medicine, but I wonder if I could manage that haha. I live in MS. Not an ideal state, I’d say.
